Mumbai, the commercial and financial capital of India, has the highest number of skyscrapers and high-rise buildings in India. More than 200 skyscrapers and 4,000[1] high-rise buildings have already been constructed in the city of Mumbai. (A skyscraper is defined as a continuously habitable high-rise building that has over 40 floors and is taller than approximately 150 metres (492 ft) according to international standards.)

The first skyscrapers in Mumbai were constructed during the 1970s, when Usha Kiran and Matru Mandir were developed and stood at about 76 metres (250 feet), or 25 floors, each. After a significant lull, construction projects since the mid-1990s began taking the skyline upwards, with a major acceleration in the pace of development since 2000, when the Lower Parel area began developing. Palais Royale structurally topped out in 2018 and is the tallest building in the country with a height of 320 meters.

Tallest buildings in Mumbai, India





![](image)Mumbai's Lower Parel Skyline
![](image)Mumbai's Skyline across Back Bay
Mumbai, the commercial and financial capital of India, has the highest number of skyscrapers and high-rise buildings in India. More than 200 skyscrapers and 4,000[1] high-rise buildings have already been constructed in the city of Mumbai. (A skyscraper is defined as a continuously habitable high-rise building that has over 40 floors and is taller than approximately 150 metres (492 ft) according to international standards.)

The first skyscrapers in Mumbai were constructed during the 1970s, when Usha Kiran and Matru Mandir were developed and stood at about 76 metres (250 feet), or 25 floors, each. After a significant lull, construction projects since the mid-1990s began taking the skyline upwards, with a major acceleration in the pace of development since 2000, when the Lower Parel area began developing. Palais Royale structurally topped out in 2018 and is the tallest building in the country with a height of 320 meters.

**Supernova Spira** is a mixed use skyscraper in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India being developed by Supertech.[3] It is located in Sector 94, Amrapali Marg, Noida. At 300 meters and 80 floors it is the tallest tower in northern India and the second tallest skyscraper in India.[4]



## Construction updates

[edit]

* As of October 2015, construction of Supernova Spira [5] has been completed by 40%, almost 34 floors.
* As of January 2016, construction of Supernova Spira has completed 38 floors.
* As of June 2018, construction of Supernova Spira has reached more than 200 meters having 58 floors completed.
* As of July 2020, construction of Supernova Spira has been completed up to the 74th floor.
* Expected completion date is by late 2024.

<content>
21-story building in New Delhi, India







| Palika Kendra |

| ![](image)Palika Kendra, a prominent example of Brutalist architecture

| ![Map](image) |
| General information |
| Type | Government Building |
| Location | New Delhi, India |

The **Palika Kendra** is a 21-story building on Sansad Marg, New Delhi, India. Designed by Kuldip Singh and Mahendra Raj, it is among the few structures in Delhi that feature Brutalist architecture. After its inauguration in 1984 with a height of 91 metres (299 ft), it remained one of the tallest buildings in Delhi for years. It serves as the headquarters of the New Delhi Municipal Council and hosts the main server and the command and control centre of the civic body.


The Palika Kendra is among 62 buildings and structures that the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage is trying to get designated as modern heritages of the post-independent India. On the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi on 31 January 2019, the Vice President of India, Venkaiah Naidu, inaugurated a grand wall mural of Gandhi made up of terracotta kulhars on a wall of the building.




## Construction

[edit]

The plot where the Palika Kendra stands used to host a tin shed that contained a small makeshift cinema hall for the entertainment of construction workers, who had been employed for developing and building the new capital of the British Raj.[1] In the early 1930s, a building was inaugurated at this site for hosting the town hall of the New Delhi Municipal Committee.[2] The town hall was demolished in the 1970s to make room for the new headquarters of the civic body.[2] The Palika Kendra was designed by two renowned architects of India, Kuldip Singh (architect) and Mahendra Raj.[3]


Inaugurated in 1984, the Palika Kendra remains one of the few structures in India that features the Brutalist architecture style.[4][5] There are 23 buildings from India that are included in the *Atlas of Brutalist Architecture*—a "comprehensive volume" documenting this architectural style from across the world.[6] With a height of 91 metres (299 ft), it remained one of the tallest buildings in Delhi for many years after its construction.[2][7]



## NDMC Headquarters

[edit]

The Palika Kendra is situated at Sansad Marg, New Delhi, and houses the headquarters of the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC). It is the tallest building owned by the NDMC.[8] The main server and the command and control centre of the civic body are also located in the building. Public places under the jurisdiction of the NDMC, where video surveillance cameras are installed, are monitored from the command and control centre by computer professionals and Delhi Police personnel.[9]


During the COVID-19 pandemic in India, in May 2020, the headquarters was sealed for two days to be sanitised and disinfected after nine NDMC employees were found to be infected with the coronavirus.[10]



## Modern heritage

[edit]

The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) approached the Heritage Conservation Committee (HCC) of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in 2013 to designate 62 buildings and structures in Delhi—including the Palika Kendra—as "modern heritage", which would bring them under the protection of the Delhi Building Bylaws, 1983. These buildings had been constructed in Delhi after 1947 and are considered contemporary architectural heritages by different organisations, including the INTACH. Though the committee agreed with the proposal, it did not take any action on it for years. This attracted criticism from the High Court of Delhi in 2016, when the court heard a petition filed by the Delhi chapter of the INTACH related to the responsibilities of the HCC and the Delhi Urban Art Commission in providing protection to post-independence modern architectural heritages.[11][12]



## Mural of Mahatma Gandhi

[edit]

A grand mural depicting Mahatma Gandhi made up of terracotta kulhars on a wall of the building was unveiled by the Vice President of India, Venkaiah Naidu, in the presence of Union Minister Giriraj Singh and the Member of Parliament from New Delhi, Meenakshi Lekhi, during the celebration of the Gandhi Jayanti on 31 January 2019. The 150-square-metre (1,600 sq ft) mural was designed to pay tribute to Gandhi on his 150th birth anniversary. A total of 3,870 kulhars, made by 150 potters from a mixture of soil collected from different parts of the country, were used in constructing this mural.[13]

<title>Palika Kendra</title>
<content>
21-story building in New Delhi, India







| Palika Kendra |
| --- |
| ![](image)Palika Kendra, a prominent example of Brutalist architecture
 |
| ![Map](image) |
| General information |
| Type | Government Building |
| Location | New Delhi, India |
| Coordinates | 28°37′42″N 77°12′55″E﻿ / ﻿28.62833°N 77.21528°E﻿ / 28.62833; 77.21528 |
| Completed | 1984 |
| Owner | New Delhi Municipal Council |
| Technical details |
| Floor count | 21 |
| Design and construction |
| Architect | Kuldip Singh (architect) |
| Structural engineer | Mahendra Raj |
| Website |
| www.ndmc.gov.in |


The **Palika Kendra** is a 21-story building on Sansad Marg, New Delhi, India. Designed by Kuldip Singh and Mahendra Raj, it is among the few structures in Delhi that feature Brutalist architecture. After its inauguration in 1984 with a height of 91 metres (299 ft), it remained one of the tallest buildings in Delhi for years. It serves as the headquarters of the New Delhi Municipal Council and hosts the main server and the command and control centre of the civic body.


The Palika Kendra is among 62 buildings and structures that the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage is trying to get designated as modern heritages of the post-independent India. On the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi on 31 January 2019, the Vice President of India, Venkaiah Naidu, inaugurated a grand wall mural of Gandhi made up of terracotta kulhars on a wall of the building.




## Construction

[edit]

The plot where the Palika Kendra stands used to host a tin shed that contained a small makeshift cinema hall for the entertainment of construction workers, who had been employed for developing and building the new capital of the British Raj.[1] In the early 1930s, a building was inaugurated at this site for hosting the town hall of the New Delhi Municipal Committee.[2] The town hall was demolished in the 1970s to make room for the new headquarters of the civic body.[2] The Palika Kendra was designed by two renowned architects of India, Kuldip Singh (architect) and Mahendra Raj.[3]


Inaugurated in 1984, the Palika Kendra remains one of the few structures in India that features the Brutalist architecture style.[4][5] There are 23 buildings from India that are included in the *Atlas of Brutalist Architecture*—a "comprehensive volume" documenting this architectural style from across the world.[6] With a height of 91 metres (299 ft), it remained one of the tallest buildings in Delhi for many years after its construction.[2][7]



## NDMC Headquarters

[edit]

The Palika Kendra is situated at Sansad Marg, New Delhi, and houses the headquarters of the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC). It is the tallest building owned by the NDMC.[8] The main server and the command and control centre of the civic body are also located in the building. Public places under the jurisdiction of the NDMC, where video surveillance cameras are installed, are monitored from the command and control centre by computer professionals and Delhi Police personnel.[9]


During the COVID-19 pandemic in India, in May 2020, the headquarters was sealed for two days to be sanitised and disinfected after nine NDMC employees were found to be infected with the coronavirus.[10]



## Modern heritage

[edit]

The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) approached the Heritage Conservation Committee (HCC) of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in 2013 to designate 62 buildings and structures in Delhi—including the Palika Kendra—as "modern heritage", which would bring them under the protection of the Delhi Building Bylaws, 1983. These buildings had been constructed in Delhi after 1947 and are considered contemporary architectural heritages by different organisations, including the INTACH. Though the committee agreed with the proposal, it did not take any action on it for years. This attracted criticism from the High Court of Delhi in 2016, when the court heard a petition filed by the Delhi chapter of the INTACH related to the responsibilities of the HCC and the Delhi Urban Art Commission in providing protection to post-independence modern architectural heritages.[11][12]



## Mural of Mahatma Gandhi

[edit]

A grand mural depicting Mahatma Gandhi made up of terracotta kulhars on a wall of the building was unveiled by the Vice President of India, Venkaiah Naidu, in the presence of Union Minister Giriraj Singh and the Member of Parliament from New Delhi, Meenakshi Lekhi, during the celebration of the Gandhi Jayanti on 31 January 2019. The 150-square-metre (1,600 sq ft) mural was designed to pay tribute to Gandhi on his 150th birth anniversary. A total of 3,870 kulhars, made by 150 potters from a mixture of soil collected from different parts of the country, were used in constructing this mural.[13]

This **list of tallest buildings in Bengaluru** ranks high-rise buildings and skyscrapers in Bengaluru, India.


Bengaluru is witnessing a huge high-rise boom with many skyscrapers being built in different parts of the city. Being the technology capital of India makes it one of the fastest growing mega cities in the world. The influx of high-skilled individuals from all parts of India come here for job and business opportunities. This is the reason why there is always demand for office and living space within the city and as a result Bengaluru is moving towards vertical development. CNTC Presidential Tower (topped-out in early 2023) is currently the tallest building in the city. It is 161 metres (528 ft) tall and has 50 floors. The World Trade Center (topped out in 2010) is currently the tallest commercial building in the city. It is 128 metres (420 ft) tall and has 32 floors. The World Trade Center, the UB Tower, the Mantri DSK Pinnacle, and Phoenix One Bangalore West are some of the various prominent skyscrapers in the city. 


As of now there are almost 1,500[1] high-rise buildings and 2 skyscrapers that have already been constructed in Bengaluru and many more high-rise buildings are currently under construction in the city right now.

![](image)UB Tower
![UB CITY](image)Bangalore's skyline viewed from Central Business District
![](image)CNTC Presidential Tower, the tallest residential Tower in Bengaluru
![UB City](image)Bangalore's Skyline viewed from Central Business District during the night
![Image taken from ISKON](image)Bangalore's skyline viewed from Yeshwantpur
This **list of tallest buildings in Bengaluru** ranks high-rise buildings and skyscrapers in Bengaluru, India.


Bengaluru is witnessing a huge high-rise boom with many skyscrapers being built in different parts of the city. Being the technology capital of India makes it one of the fastest growing mega cities in the world. The influx of high-skilled individuals from all parts of India come here for job and business opportunities. This is the reason why there is always demand for office and living space within the city and as a result Bengaluru is moving towards vertical development. CNTC Presidential Tower (topped-out in early 2023) is currently the tallest building in the city. It is 161 metres (528 ft) tall and has 50 floors. The World Trade Center (topped out in 2010) is currently the tallest commercial building in the city. It is 128 metres (420 ft) tall and has 32 floors. The World Trade Center, the UB Tower, the Mantri DSK Pinnacle, and Phoenix One Bangalore West are some of the various prominent skyscrapers in the city. 


As of now there are almost 1,500[1] high-rise buildings and 2 skyscrapers that have already been constructed in Bengaluru and many more high-rise buildings are currently under construction in the city right now.

![](image)*My Home Avatar, View from Outer Ring Road*
![](image)Offices and residential complex seen from Khajaguda lake



This **list of tallest buildings in Hyderabad[1]** lists the high-rises in Hyderabad, India.


Hyderabad is witnessing a massive construction boom around its IT corridor with several high-rise & skyscraper proposals getting approvals as there is huge demand for office and living space in the city.[2]


Several high-rises are already constructed in areas like Gachibowli, HITEC City, Raidurg, Kondapur, Manikonda, Kukatpally and numerous other buildings are currently under construction. Many real estate developments are taking place in newly planned areas like Neopolis, Kokapet and Gandipet. As of January 2023, Lodha Bellezza Towers 3, 4 & 5 (45 floors, 153 metres) are the tallest completed buildings of Hyderabad. The tallest project under-construction is Candeur Skyline with 4 towers with a height of 244 meters. 



All the data mentioned in the below lists are from verified government sources.

![](image)LANCO Hills captured from Chitrapuri colony road

![](image)*My Home Avatar, View from Outer Ring Road*
![](image)Offices and residential complex seen from Khajaguda lake



This **list of tallest buildings in Hyderabad[1]** lists the high-rises in Hyderabad, India.


Hyderabad is witnessing a massive construction boom around its IT corridor with several high-rise & skyscraper proposals getting approvals as there is huge demand for office and living space in the city.[2]


Several high-rises are already constructed in areas like Gachibowli, HITEC City, Raidurg, Kondapur, Manikonda, Kukatpally and numerous other buildings are currently under construction. Many real estate developments are taking place in newly planned areas like Neopolis, Kokapet and Gandipet. As of January 2023, Lodha Bellezza Towers 3, 4 & 5 (45 floors, 153 metres) are the tallest completed buildings of Hyderabad. The tallest project under-construction is Candeur Skyline with 4 towers with a height of 244 meters. 



All the data mentioned in the below lists are from verified government sources.

![](image)LANCO Hills captured from Chitrapuri colony road

Now we need to present answer. Provide table with city, tallest building name, height, floors, year completed, use. Use data from sources.

We have Mumbai: World One (280.2m, 76 floors, 2020). Also Palais Royale (320m but still under construction). Use completed: World One.

Delhi: Palika Kendra 91m (21 floors, 1984) but taller is Supernova Spira in Noida (300m, 80 floors) but not Delhi proper. Could mention that the tallest building within Delhi district is Palika Kendra. Provide both.

Bangalore: CNTC Presidential Tower 161m, 50 floors, 2023.

Hyderabad: Lodha Bellezza Tower 4 (153m, 45 floors, 2023).

Ahmedabad: The 31st (133.75m, 32 floors, 2022).

Now compile.

content:
**Tallest building in each of India’s five most‑populous cities (2024)**  

| Rank (by city population) | City (2023‑24 estimate) | Tallest building **in the city proper** | Height* | Floors | Year completed / topped‑out | Primary use | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Mumbai** (≈ 20 M) | **World One** – Lodha Group | **280.2 m** (919 ft) | 76 | 2020 (topped‑out; occupied 2022) | Residential (luxury apartments) | “World One” entry in *List of tallest buildings in Mumbai* |
| **2** | **Delhi** (≈ 19 M) | **Palika Kendra** (NDMC headquarters) | **91 m** (299 ft) | 21 | 1984 | Government/office | “Palika Kendra” article (height 91 m) |
| | | *(Note: the tallest structure in the National Capital Region is **Supernova Spira** in Noida – 300 m, 80 floors, under construction; it lies outside the Delhi municipal limits.)* | | | | | “Supernova Spira” page (roof height 300 m) |
| **3** | **Bengaluru** (≈ 12 M) | **CNTC Presidential Tower** | **161 m** (528 ft) | 50 | 2023 (topped‑out) | Residential | “CNTC Presidential Tower” entry in *List of tallest buildings in Bengaluru* |
| **4** | **Hyderabad** (≈ 10 M) | **Lodha Bellezza Tower 4** (Kukatpally) | **153 m** (502 ft) | 45 | 2023 (completed) | Residential | “Lodha Bellezza Tower 4” entry in *List of tallest buildings in Hyderabad* |
| **5** | **Ahmedabad** (≈ 8 M) | **The 31st** (residential tower) | **133.75 m** (439 ft) | 32 | 2022 (completed) | Residential | “The 31st” entry in *List of tallest buildings in Ahmedabad* |

\* Height refers to **architectural height** (including spires, excluding antenna masts).  

### Quick notes  

* **Mumbai** remains the city with the tallest completed skyscraper in India.  The newer “Palais Royale” (≈ 320 m) is still under construction, so **World One** is the tallest *completed* building.  
* **Delhi** has relatively few high‑rises because of strict height‑restriction rules.  The 21‑storey **Palika Kendra** (91 m) is the tallest building within the Delhi municipal area.  The much taller **Supernova Spira** (300 m, 80 floors) is located in Noida, part of the broader NCR but not within Delhi’s limits.  
* **Bengaluru’s** skyline is dominated by residential towers; the **CNTC Presidential Tower** (161 m) overtook the former record‑holder Mantri DSK Pinnacle in 2023.  
* **Hyderabad**’s rapid IT‑corridor boom has produced several 150 m+ towers.  The **Lodha Bellezza** complex (Tower 4/5) at 153 m is currently the tallest completed building.  
* **Ahmedabad**’s high‑rise market is still emerging; the 32‑storey **The 31st** at 133.75 m (finished 2022) tops the city’s list.  

All figures are taken from the latest Wikipedia “List of tallest buildings” pages for each city (accessed Nov 2025).
